title: Diagrid Catalyst 2.0 Adds Durable and Verifiable Execution for AI Agents
gist: Diagrid's Catalyst 2.0 (announced 28 July 2026) layers Dapr-based durable execution and cryptographically signed workflow history onto ten third-party agent frameworks (LangGraph, Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, etc.), positioning itself as a cross-framework reliability and audit layer against Temporal, Restate and native LangGraph persistence. The author flags that Diagrid's '10x faster than open-source Dapr' claim is unverifiable as stated and that attestation proves history integrity, not agent correctness.

themes.theme: Cross-framework durability layer as product wedge

insights.claim: Diagrid Catalyst 2.0 ships integrations with ten agent frameworks — LangGraph, LangGraph Deep Agents, Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, Dapr Agents, AWS Strands, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Managed Agents, CrewAI and Pydantic AI — betting on framework-agnostic infrastructure rather than owning the agent framework itself.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: The agent-infrastructure land grab is moving to the neutral middleware layer; watch whether framework vendors bundle equivalent durability and squeeze independents.
insights.locator: Ten framework integrations ship in the release

insights.claim: Catalyst applies checkpointing at the granularity of individual model and tool calls, so an interrupted multi-step agent run resumes without re-paying for already-completed LLM calls — directly attacking the cost of retrying long agent sequences.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Token-cost waste from failed long runs is a real enterprise pain point; call-level durability is a monetizable efficiency layer as agent runs get longer and pricier.
insights.quote: a long multi-step run fails late in the sequence and, without checkpointing at call granularity, the retry re-pays for every model call already completed

insights.claim: Catalyst's differentiation versus Temporal, Restate and LangGraph's own persistence is not durability per se but a single Dapr-based recovery-plus-attestation model spanning many frameworks, with durability at individual model/tool calls rather than LangGraph's graph-superstep boundaries.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Durable-execution is a contested market (Temporal, Restate already host agent workflows); the buying decision reduces to where recovery, identity and audit evidence should live — a useful lens for sizing vendors.
insights.quote: Catalyst is neither the first durability option for these frameworks nor a new entrant to a thin market.
insights.locator: Catalyst is neither the first durability

insights.claim: Dapr 1.18 introduces signed workflow history: batches of history events are hashed, digests chained to the preceding signature, and signed with the sidecar's SPIFFE-based identity, making deleted, reordered or modified agent execution history detectable and verifiable outside the producing application via the Dapr Sentry trust anchor.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Tamper-evident agent audit trails are becoming an infrastructure primitive — a prerequisite for regulated-industry agent adoption and a likely compliance checkbox in enterprise AI procurement.
insights.locator: The verification model comes from Dapr 1.18

insights.claim: Demand for agent auditability is being framed by vendors as 'proof of what happened' when agents call tools or delegate work, per Diagrid CTO Yaron Schneider, who also chairs the Agentic AI Foundation's Workflows and Process Integration Working Group — signaling standards-body capture of the agent-workflow layer.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: A vendor CTO chairing the relevant standards working group suggests Dapr-style attestation could become the de facto standard; standards position often precedes commercial moat.

insights.claim: Cryptographic attestation of agent workflow history proves integrity and provenance of the recorded log only — not that the agent decided correctly, that tools returned accurate data, or that every external side effect was captured.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Buyers may over-read 'verifiable agents' marketing; the correctness/assurance gap leaves room for eval, guardrail and observability vendors on top of attestation layers.
insights.quote: Cryptographic attestation proves the integrity and provenance of recorded history, not that an agent made a correct decision

insights.claim: Workflow history signing in Dapr 1.18 is disabled by default behind a feature flag, hard-requires mTLS (daprd refuses to start otherwise), and is a one-way, per-workflow decision — no retroactive signing and toggling mid-run is a verification error — so real-world adoption friction is material.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Operational friction means signed-history adoption will lag the headline feature; expect slow enterprise rollout and services revenue around migration.
insights.locator: Teams should note that signing is disabled

insights.claim: Diagrid claims Catalyst delivers up to 10x the performance of open-source Dapr and supports millions of concurrent agent workflows, but does not specify whether the multiple is throughput, starts-per-second or latency, nor the workload or configuration measured — the claim cannot be independently assessed.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Treat vendor performance multiples in the agent-infra space as marketing until benchmarked; diligence should demand workload-specified benchmarks.
insights.quote: the comparison cannot be independently assessed

insights.claim: Diagrid monetizes via pricing tiers sized by concurrent workflows — free cloud, dedicated-cloud, bring-your-own-cloud, and a custom-quoted Enterprise Server for on-premise and air-gapped deployments — an open-core play layered on Dapr with concurrency as the metering unit.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Concurrent-workflow metering ties revenue directly to agent proliferation inside customers; a clean proxy metric for agent adoption if disclosed.

insights.claim: Practitioners evaluating Catalyst must still assess retry handling for non-idempotent tools, storage and latency overhead, certificate rotation, independent verification, and the open-source-Dapr versus commercial-Catalyst capability split.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: A ready-made diligence checklist for the durable-agent-execution category; the open-vs-commercial boundary is the key open-core risk to probe.
insights.locator: Practitioners should also assess retry handling

insights.claim: Named enterprise adoption of Catalyst is thin so far: only optics manufacturer ZEISS Group is cited, positioning Catalyst as a stable foundation for both AI and traditional workloads amid rapidly churning AI frameworks.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: One named reference customer is a weak proof point; watch for logo accumulation as the real adoption signal in this category.
insights.quote: a rapidly evolving landscape of AI models and frameworks, Catalyst provides the stable foundation we can rely on

insights.claim: Enterprises are hedging AI-framework churn by anchoring on infrastructure abstractions: ZEISS explicitly values Catalyst because agent frameworks are evolving too fast to bet a platform on any single one.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Framework-volatility hedging favors neutral runtime/middleware vendors over framework vendors — a durable thesis for where enterprise agent budgets settle.

insights.claim: Catalyst runs in cloud, on-premise and air-gapped environments, with durable agents built in a Python SDK and workflow SDK support listed for .NET, Go, Java, JavaScript and Python (Rust in open-source Dapr 1.18) — deliberately covering regulated and sovereign deployment demands.
insights.speaker: Mark Silvester
insights.so_what: Air-gapped support targets defense/regulated buyers where agent auditability sells hardest; polyglot SDK coverage widens the enterprise funnel.
insights.locator: Diagrid says Catalyst runs in cloud
